math_recheck: 1e9/3 = 333,333,333/day; /86,400 = 3,858.02/s. Correct. One $1 cup per dollar = 3,858 cups. Correct. Say-word count = 71 (not 74): 9+8+7+11+9+8+9+10. At 0.9 speed (about 2.1 w/s) this is about 34 s: inside the limit but with no slack.

viewer_notes.bait_and_switch: Partly. The hook promises YOU earn $3,000 a second. Line 2 puts you at a $1 lemonade stand, but the money never goes to you: it goes to a register 'next door', then to GTA 5. The viewer who stayed for 'what if I earned that' is given a sales stat about a company, and line 6/7 turn the 'you' into the loser. The stakes are borrowed, not delivered. Fix: make the viewer the earner (see fixes) or change the hook to a question about the game.
viewer_notes.payoff_surprise: Weak. The hook already says three thousand a second; line 5 only confirms it (3,858 vs 3,000). The only new information is the cup conversion, but that is the same number again because a cup costs $1 ('3,858 cups' = '$3,858'). Lines 5, 6, 7 all repeat one number.
viewer_notes.hedges_ip: Hedges are good: 'about', 'estimated sales' badge, and the description says estimated retail. Remaining issues: 'earned' in the hook and 'made' in line 4 treat revenue as income; the figure is retail sales, not profit. IP is clean: plain text 'GTA', generic register, no Rockstar assets.

fixes: Line 1 + lines 2-3 (stakes, 6): the 'you' never earns the money. Make the viewer the earner: keep the hook, then line 2 'Your lemonade stand sells one cup every second.' and have the story be 'GTA 5 sold as if it were your stand'. Or reword the hook to 'What if you sold a game that earned three thousand dollars every second?' so the hook and story match.

Line 5 (payoff/surprise, 6): it only confirms the hook's number. Hold the exact rate back: say a rounded or smaller figure in the hook (or no figure) and reveal a bigger, new comparison at the end, e.g. per day ($333 million), or 'in the time you read this line, it made about $30,000' (3,858 x 8 s = $30,864). Delete the rate repetition in line 7 (cups = dollars, no new information).

Line 6 (escalation, 6): 'You try to count, but cannot keep up' adds no information. Replace it with a new fact or twist (e.g. what the second-by-second pace means over his lemonade day: one dollar a cup, 3,858 cups, he needs 1 hour to sell 3,600 cups at a cup a second) or cut it and use the time for a payoff line.

Lines 3-4 (open loop, 6): the answer (GTA 5) lands at roughly 13 s, which is the midpoint. Move 'GTA 5' to line 3 as the reveal question, and plant a real question at 3 s ('Who earns that much?') that is answered only in line 7-8.

Line 8 (ending, 6): 'Will GTA 6 beat it?' is ambiguous (beat what: the record, the rate, the 3 days?) and has an obvious answer, so it is weak comment bait. Use a clear A/B: 'Would you sell lemonade or a game? Comment lemonade or game.' or 'GTA 6 sells in three days. More or less than one billion?'

Line 4 (facts, 8): 'made one billion dollars' is revenue (retail sales). Say 'sold about one billion dollars' of games; also change the hook 'earned' to match. Source says 'over $1 billion', so 'about' is OK but 'over' is the safer wording.

Clarity (8): line 5 'three thousand, eight hundred fifty-eight dollars' is a long number string for a non-native listener at 0.9 speed; round it to 'almost four thousand dollars' in speech and keep the exact $3,858 on screen. Line 3 'a giant register opens next door' is an odd image: 'a giant cash register appears' reads more clearly. Length: 71 words at 0.9 speed is about 34 s; cut one short line to leave margin below 35 s.

Hook (7): the opener is the right format and the counter visual is good, but 9 spoken words, then a cut to a lemonade story with a $1 price, lowers the tension. Show the register in frame 0 so the picture answers 'who earns that?' quickly. Originality (7) and entertainment (7): the lemonade vs register gag is fine but repeats the 'tiny $1 stand' idea from rejected test #1 ('The $1 Jar'); add a physical gag with a consequence (the register's cash blows Benny's stand away) rather than a comparison bar.

UPLOAD block: title 'What If You Earned $3,858 Every Second?' gives away the exact number (no curiosity gap) and does not match the spoken hook ('three thousand'); use 'What If You Earned $3,000 Every Second? #Shorts' or hint at the twist ('...and Still Lost To GTA?'). Description line 1 'A lemonade stand vs the money GTA 5 made every single second.' is a real hook and not a copy of the title: OK. Line 2 comment question is present: OK (but fix per Line 8 if changed). Money topic: 'Not financial advice.' is missing; add it (the rubric requires it for money topics). Hashtags: 5 (#gta6 #gta5 #gaming #money #Shorts) is within 3-5 and relevant, 1 emoji: OK. Tags: 9 phrases, fine; 'gta 6 release date' and 'gta 6 hype' are only loosely connected to this video, replace with 'gta 5 sales record' or 'money per second'. Upload gaps are fix notes, not hard-gate fails.
